command: llvm-mc -triple=aarch64 -filetype=obj A64-P10-sub-family.s -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Input (151 B, LF, trailing newline), one instruction per line with two leading spaces: `sub x3, x4, x5` / `sub x6, x7, #4095` / `sub x9, x10, #291, lsl #12` / `sub x12, x13, x14, lsl #3` / `sub x15, x16, x17, lsr #7` / `sub x18, x19, x20, asr #63`. One instruction per `sub` row: the unshifted register row, both `sh` values of the immediate row, and all three shift keywords. Every row uses distinct registers, so a register-field slip cannot hide behind another row; the immediate row is exercised at 4095 (all twelve bits set) and at 291 with `lsl #12` (field content, not the pre-scaled literal); `lsr #7` and `asr #63` move bits 23-22 and pin the top of `imm6`. `llvm-mc -show-encoding` prints `sub x3, x4, x5` for the first line, i.e. the `-lsl0` spelling. Every operand is a register or an immediate, so `llvm-readobj -r` prints an empty relocation list and no linker is involved.
source: Arm MRS SUB_64_addsub_shift and SUB_64_addsub_imm (op at 30+1 = 1, shift at 22+2, imm6 at 10+6, sh at 22+1, imm12 at 10+12); measured in EXP-0019 §2
